title: Noach: laws for everyone (Genesis 9:1–7)
hookLine: the rabbis drew seven laws for all humanity from Noah's covenant

lines: A COVENANT WITH ALL OF THEM.
cards: The ark has landed. The ground is drying. Noah and his family step out onto an empty earth, the animals scattering into the hills.
Everyone alive on the planet is in this one small group. Whatever comes next, every nation, every language, every person who will ever live, starts here. So what does God say to them first?
Not a law for one people. A covenant with all of them, and through them with everyone.

teach.h: FOR IN THE IMAGE OF GOD MADE HE MAN.
teach.b: God blesses Noah and his sons: be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth. The animals are given as food, but with a limit: don't eat flesh with its life, its blood, still in it.
Then the heart of it: "Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed; for in the image of God made He man." The verse grounds the worth of every human life in God's image.
A few verses later comes the rainbow, the sign that the flood will never come again.

teach.h: SEVEN LAWS FOR THE CHILDREN OF NOAH.
teach.b: From these verses, and a few others, the rabbis of the Talmud drew seven basic laws for all humanity, called the laws of the children of Noah.
Six are things not to do: no idolatry, no cursing God, no murder, no sexual immorality, no theft, and no eating a limb torn from a living animal.

teach.h: SIX DON'TS AND ONE DO: COURTS.
teach.b: One is something to do: set up courts of justice. Every person on earth, in this view, is a child of Noah, and these are the basic decencies God asks of everyone.
In this tradition, the Torah's commandments as a whole are for Jews; for everyone else, these seven.
And in the Tosefta, Rabbi Joshua teaches that the righteous of the nations have a share in the world to come. So, in this view, no one needs to become Jewish to be righteous.
The seven laws are a Jewish framework, drawn from a Jewish reading of the text. But look at most of the list: don't kill, don't steal, don't be cruel to animals, have courts.
Much of it reads like a floor of basic decency.

how: Jewish law teaches seven Noahide laws as the basic obligations God asks of all humanity, and, following Rabbi Joshua in the Tosefta, holds that the righteous of every nation have a share in the world to come.

games.q: the flood is over. Noah's family steps out onto an empty earth. what does God give them first?
o: a law for one people only.
a blessing and a covenant with all humanity.
a warning to stay in the ark.
games.why: be fruitful and multiply, a limit on eating blood, the sacredness of every life, and the rainbow: a covenant with everyone.

practice: Think of the most different person you can imagine: far away, another language, another faith, another life.
Ask what you share, not beliefs but basic decencies: don't take a life, don't take what isn't yours, be fair, be kind to animals. Let each one come slowly, and picture that person keeping them too.
